turns.content: ok so, when does a pattern of oversights stop being just accidents. like, you always forget someone's dietary needs at every single family dinner, and you never add them to the group chat, even after a year. at what point is it just, you know, a pattern.

Yeah—**you don’t have to prove it’s deliberate for it to count as a pattern.** If someone’s dietary needs keep getting forgotten and they’re still left out of the group chat after a year, those aren’t just unrelated incidents anymore.

The useful distinction is between **intent and responsiveness**: once someone knows there’s a problem, do they make an effort to fix it? Do they add the person to the chat, ask what they can eat, put a reminder somewhere? Or does each incident get treated like the first time it’s ever come up?

Repeated oversights don’t necessarily prove “we want to exclude you.” But they can communicate “including you isn’t getting our attention”—and that hurts even without malicious intent.

If you want to name it, you could say:
> “I’m not saying you’re doing this on purpose. I’m saying it keeps happening, even after I’ve brought it up, and it leaves me excluded. I need something to change, not just an explanation for this one time.”

You’re allowed to take the repetition seriously without first solving what’s in everyone’s head.

I need concrete changes: include me in the chat and make sure there’s food I can safely eat when I’m invited. Another apology without follow-through won’t address this.
